_comment: Canonical Meshtastic bearer wire contract, shared by bearers/apple/HopBearerMeshtastic
(MeshtasticWire.swift) and bearers/android/bearer-meshtastic (MeshtasticWire.kt). Like the BLE
dial-backoff table, this exists because bearers are per-platform packages with no shared core: the
two Meshtastic implementations must agree byte for byte or an Apple phone and an Android phone on
the same LoRa mesh cannot talk. tools/meshtastic-parity.sh fails CI if either side drifts from
these values.
hop_portnum: the Meshtastic PortNum Hop rides, inside the PRIVATE_APP range (256..511).
admin_portnum: PortNum.ADMIN_APP. Channel get/set rides this, never the Hop port.
hop_channel_*: Hop writes a SECONDARY Meshtastic channel (never PRIMARY/index 0) named Hop with a
shared AES-128 PSK so two Hop phones interoperate without a QR. Role 2 is SECONDARY. Max slots 8.
max_chunk / frag_header: a Hop link frame is split into fragments of at most max_chunk bytes, each
prefixed with a frag_header of [msgId:2][fragIndex:1][fragCount:1]. These two numbers ARE the
fragmentation contract; fragment_vectors pins the resulting fragment count for a set of frame
sizes so a change to max_chunk that silently reshapes the wire is caught.
frames: the 1-byte Hop link-frame type tags. ack (0x04) is Meshtastic-bearer-only: a unicast
receipt for one reassembled Hop frame (msgId). hello/ping/pong/data stay identical to LAN/BLE.
routing_portnum: Meshtastic ROUTING_APP. Unicast fragments set want_ack; a Routing error_reason
NONE on this port is the radio ACK. Hop still sprays until the Hop ack frame, because a mesh ACK
is per MeshPacket fragment, not per Hop frame, and Meshtastic does not store-and-forward by default.
spray_*: exponential resend of an unacked unicast DATA/HELLO. Interval starts at spray_initial_ms,
doubles each miss, caps at spray_cap_ms, never gives up while the link is up. Tick is 1s so the
first retry is not delayed by the 30s ping timer. max_outstanding bounds in-flight sprays per dest.
ping_ms / dead_ms: the keepalive cadence and liveness deadline (Swift declares seconds, Kotlin
declares milliseconds; the guard scales before comparing so a seconds/millis mixup cannot pass).
